The '''2012–13 [[Cypriot First Division]]''' was the 74th season of the [[Cyprus|Cypriot]] top-level [[Association football|football]] league. It began on 1 September 2012 and ended on 19 May 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cfa.com.cy/Gr/news/10116 |script-title=el:Αρχές Σεπτεμβρίου η πρεμιέρα του νέου Πρωταθλήματος |language=el |publisher=CFA |date=2012-05-08 |access-date=2012-05-18}}</ref> [[AEL Limassol]] were the defending champions. [[APOEL FC|APOEL]] won the championship two matchweeks before the end of the season.

The league comprise eleven teams from the [[2011–12 Cypriot First Division|2011–12 season]] and three promoted teams from the [[2011–12 Cypriot Second Division|2011–12 Second Division]].

==Teams==
[[Ermis Aradippou]] and [[Anagennisi Dherynia]] were relegated at the end of the first stage of the [[2011–12 Cypriot First Division|2011–12 season]] after finishing in the bottom two places of the table. They were joined by [[Aris Limassol F.C.|Aris Limassol]], who finished at the bottom of the second-phase Group C.

The relegated teams were replaced by [[2011–12 Cypriot Second Division|2011–12 Second Division]] champions [[Doxa Katokopias F.C.|Doxa Katokopias]], runners-up [[Ayia Napa F.C.|Ayia Napa]] and third-placed team [[AEP Paphos F.C.|AEP Paphos]].

===Relegation play-offs===
The 11th-placed team [[Nea Salamis Famagusta FC|Nea Salamina]] faced 4th-placed [[2012–13 Cypriot Second Division]] side [[Anagennisi Dherynia]], in a single-legged play-off for one spot in the [[2013–14 Cypriot First Division]]. The match was held at [[Antonis Papadopoulos Stadium]] on 23 May 2013 and [[Nea Salamis Famagusta FC|Nea Salamina]] won by 3–0, retaining its [[Cypriot First Division]] spot for the 2013–14 season.
